final.title: Why data cleaning is not the whole job
final.body:
Data cleaning helps, but it is not the whole workflow.

If your team fixes fields and still has to make the same downstream decisions by hand, you have only solved the input side. The real question is not “is the data clean?” It is “what still needs human judgment after the data is clean?”

That is where a lot of small-business workflows break: messy inputs on one side, decision handling on the other. Cleaning helps with the first. It does not remove the second. If a clean row still needs someone to categorise it, route it, approve it, or decide whether it is an exception, the manual work is still there. Software is very good at the boring bits. It is less good at guessing.

A practical next step is to map one repeating workflow as input → decision → output. Write down the steps, then mark which ones are rules-based and which ones need judgment or sign-off. If you find that cleaned data still leaves a long tail of manual decisions, that boundary is often where automation fits. For high-risk steps, keep human approval in place.

Start with the decision layer, not another cleanup tool.
